changes.current_line: Proven ROI, backed by an independent economic impact study.
changes.change: For finance buyers (CFO/controller) at invoice-heavy mid-market businesses: "Send us one month of your statements and we'll show you what manual matching is costing you, in your numbers, not ours." Run it as a standard working session led by a solutions engineer on the customer's own bank, processor and ERP data.
changes.why: The deal went from 'dead' at 20 percent to 'paperwork' only after a session on one month of the controller's statements, and the CFO trusted the figure because it was 'my number, not yours', the opposite of an external study.

changes.current_line: Every payout reconciles automatically to its transactions and your ERP.
changes.change: For CFOs and controllers: "Know where every deposit came from, and close the month without the archaeology." Back it with a live demo that traces one deposit to its individual transactions and into the ERP.
changes.why: Reconciliation was the only thing that drew a reaction (the CFO interrupted the demo with 'go back'), but she described it as 'where my money is', 'the deposits' and 'a week of archaeology', never as payouts or payments.

changes.current_line: Financial infrastructure to grow globally, in every currency.
changes.change: For regional, invoice-heavy businesses (e.g. multi-state distributors with small IT teams), stop opening first calls with M1 and with the M2 developer/API story. Open instead with the finance outcome (days to close, hours of manual matching, unmatched deposits). Make that outcome page one of every proposal so it holds up when it is forwarded to a CFO who never joined a call.
changes.why: The global-infrastructure opener met silence, the developer story 'went nowhere' with a four-person IT team that isn't building anything, nobody at the customer said 'infrastructure', and the CFO rejected the first proposal on page one because she saw checkout and APIs as not her problem.

changes.current_line: Trusted by leading businesses; see our customer stories.
changes.change: Add a wholesale/distribution proof point: a peer reference and case study about invoice and deposit reconciliation at a distributor, offered to finance buyers in wholesale and B2B distribution in place of retail or software stories.
changes.why: The CFO asked to speak to 'another distributor. Wholesale, invoices', dismissed the retail case study ('this is a company that sells sweaters') and raised the missing reference twice, even though she signed.
